body.x: The Daegu Center for Creative Economy & Innovation (DCCEI, CEO Han In-kook) announced that 14 promising regional companies selected for the “Startup City Project” participated in the Future Innovation Tech Expo 2026 (FIX 2026), held from October 21 to 24 at EXCO in Daegu. The initiative provided a dedicated exhibition and business-matching platform to showcase advanced innovations in artificial intelligence, robotics, and industrial deep tech to global investors, buyers, and international press delegations.

The Startup City Project is a flagship regional revitalization policy launched this year by South Korea’s Ministry of SMEs and Startups. Designed to decentralize early-stage investment and venture capital resources traditionally concentrated in the Seoul metropolitan area, the program unifies Daegu’s local industrial, academic, and technical infrastructure to foster a self-sustaining innovation ecosystem. In 2026, DCCEI selected and backed 74 regional deep-tech startups, injecting tailored commercialization capital of up to 400 million KRW for emerging future industries and up to 250 million KRW for general manufacturing and technology sectors.

At FIX 2026, DCCEI hosted a specialized corporate zone featuring 14 project beneficiaries, including Nuvinda, Yellosis, A.Cure, Zio Robot, EROP, AIEEV, LearningVision, FutureDrive, WPosition, AIRS, UNIVA, RootLab, Muaheng, and TheSunHan. The participating companies engaged with domestic and international buyers, validated product readiness, and secured customer pipelines for technologies designed for direct deployment in industrial and smart manufacturing environments.

body.cap: Image provided by Daegu Center for Creative Economy & Innovation

body.x: To accelerate global recognition, DCCEI orchestrated targeted on-site media networking and pitch sessions connecting the startups with international journalists, tech editors, and global media award judges attending the expo. During these sessions, Kijung Ju, Director of the Startup City Division at DCCEI, introduced the program’s vision and long-term milestones to overseas press delegations. From media outlets, Le Café du geek, Ubergizmo, Digitimes, ET Manufacturing, Otaku Soken, Chinabyte, Clipset, Pokde.net, CNET Korea, and IT DongA participated.

Several startups drew significant attention during the on-site press presentations for their specialized industrial applications. Nuvinda, led by CEO Hyoseok Shi, introduced its 120Nm-class high back-drivability integrated actuator, which features ultra-high torque density engineered specifically for physical AI systems, humanoid robotics, and heavy-payload industrial automation. In the enterprise computing space, TheSunHan, led by CEO David Kwon, announced the commercialization of YAK, a customized on-premises AI computing infrastructure platform built for scalable, localized deep learning workloads.

Complementing hardware and infrastructure developments, AIEEV, led by CEO Sejin Park, demonstrated Private Air Cloud, a secure enterprise inference cloud platform enabling corporations to deploy autonomous AI agents safely within protected internal network boundaries. In smart manufacturing and quality control, LearningVision, headed by CEO KwangJoon Lee, unveiled an end-to-end composite visual AI inspection solution for secondary battery cell production, integrating automated region-of-interest extraction, defect segmentation, anomaly detection, and classification.

body.cap: Kijung Ju, Startup City Division Director of DAEGU CENTER FOR CREATIVE ECONOMY & INNOVATION, introduces the Startup City Project to global media representatives and participating companies. | Photo provided by Daegu Center for Creative Economy & Innovation

body.x: DCCEI reaffirmed its commitment to scaling the Startup City Project framework by combining direct commercialization funding with strategic cross-border investment matching and continuous global media outreach. Moving forward, the center plans to deepen collaborations with international accelerators and trade partners to establish Daegu as a premier global hub for robotics, Physical AI, and next-generation deep-tech startups.
